title: Binary tensor coherence of quotient scalar composition
statement: Let T be a scheme and let ell,r,m,n be natural numbers with n ≤ m ≤ r. Write A_i = ULift (ULift (ZMod (ell^i))), F and G for ordinary derived scalar extension along A_r → A_m and A_m → A_n, and H for extension along A_r → A_n, using def-pur-finite-smooth-coefficient-arrows. Let alpha:F⋙G≅H be its canonical adjunction associator and delta the representative-normalized binary tensor comparisons of def-pur-exceptional-coefficient-normalizations. For any K,L in D(T_et,A_r), G(delta_F(K,L));delta_G(FK,FL);(alpha_K tensor alpha_L) = alpha_(K tensor L);delta_H(K,L). Composition is in application order. No root-line comparison, tensor power, relative dimension, smoothness or flat quotient hypothesis occurs.

source.place: Part (3), tensor map: scalar associativity and its binary tensor balancing subargument.

proof.text: Resolve K and L by flat-term K-flat complexes. Extension of scalars takes such representatives to flat-term K-flat complexes over the target ring. The normalization of tensorIso identifies the binary comparisons with ordinary scalar balancing. The adjunction associator is normalized by identity composition of restrictions, so on representatives it is ordinary scalar multiplication. Both composites send each homogeneous pure tensor c tensor (b tensor (p tensor q)) to the same balanced tensor in the two scalar-extended factors. The degree pair and total-complex sign are unchanged. Sheafification and localization preserve the equality of chain maps. Naturality with respect to the resolution quasi-isomorphisms gives the displayed equality for arbitrary K,L. This argument also covers equal indices, zero rings and empty schemes.

theorem quotientScalarTensorComp
    (T : Scheme.{u}) (ell : ℕ) {r m n : ℕ} (hmr : m ≤ r) (hnm : n ≤ m)
    (K L : DerivedCategoryModule (coefficient ell r) T) :
    (ordinaryScalar (FiniteReduction.quotient ell hnm) T).map
        ((ExceptionalCoefficients.tensorIso (FiniteReduction.quotient ell hmr) T).hom.app
          (K, L)) ≫
      (ExceptionalCoefficients.tensorIso (FiniteReduction.quotient ell hnm) T).hom.app
        ((ordinaryScalar (FiniteReduction.quotient ell hmr) T).obj K,
          (ordinaryScalar (FiniteReduction.quotient ell hmr) T).obj L) ≫
      ((derivedTensor (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (coefficient ell n)) T).map
        ((ordinaryAssociator T ell hmr hnm).hom.app K)).app
          ((ordinaryScalar (FiniteReduction.quotient ell hnm) T).obj
            ((ordinaryScalar (FiniteReduction.quotient ell hmr) T).obj L)) ≫
      ((derivedTensor (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (coefficient ell n)) T).obj
        ((ordinaryScalar (FiniteReduction.quotient ell (hnm.trans hmr)) T).obj K)).map
          ((ordinaryAssociator T ell hmr hnm).hom.app L) =
    (ordinaryAssociator T ell hmr hnm).hom.app
        (((derivedTensor (ModuleCat.{u + 1} (coefficient ell r)) T).obj K).obj L) ≫
      (ExceptionalCoefficients.tensorIso
        (FiniteReduction.quotient ell (hnm.trans hmr)) T).hom.app (K, L)
